02 / FINDINGS & QUESTIONS

Test the argument against the evidence

Fixed comparisons for 2021–2025. Explorer filters do not change this section.

A descriptive analysis, not a causal model. These checks address questions raised in the October 2026 motorcycle safety submission. They do not endorse its wider claims.

Where did fatal casualty counts change in 2025?

2025 compared with 2024, by casualty age. Small counts fluctuate substantially. This is a screening table for follow-up, not a ranking of causal effects.

THE NEXT EVIDENCE TO ADD

From patterns to explanations

  1. Exposure: motorcycle mileage and fleet counts, ideally matched by capacity, age and geography, to distinguish more riding from greater risk.
  2. Collision investigation: access-controlled contributory / road safety factors, case files and road geometry to investigate mechanisms.
  3. Machine and training evidence: verified ABS / MSC fitment, licence and training history, and instrumented braking studies.
  4. Evaluation: agreed hypotheses, suitable comparison groups and uncertainty estimates before attributing changes to interventions.

History provides context, not a pooled answer

Source: DfT RAS0102. The rate uses national motorcycle traffic in billion vehicle miles. It accounts for overall mileage, but not the changing mix of riders, machines or trips. Serious-injury counts in the table are unadjusted and not comparable across all recording regimes.

1999 & 2005

Vehicle categories change

Historic motorcycle categories are included in total counts. Modern engine-size groups should not be projected backwards unchanged.

From 2012

Severity recording changes

Police forces adopt injury-based reporting at different times. Use adjusted serious-injury estimates for recent comparisons.

2020

Travel disruption

The pandemic disrupted travel. A change from 2020 alone is an unsuitable measure of ordinary trend.

2024 onwards

Specification transition

Changes to manoeuvre and other fields affect comparability. Missing historic bend codes cannot be treated as “not on a bend”.

DOES THE EXTRA COMPLEXITY HELP?

Tested on 2025 records excluded from training and calibration

Brier score measures probability error; lower is better. AUC measures how well the model ranks KSI above slight injuries; 0.5 is chance ranking, 1.0 is perfect. Neither measure is “percentage accurate”. The constant baseline predicts the 2024 calibration-set KSI share for everyone.

Do the predicted probabilities match observed outcomes?

Five equally sized groups ordered by predicted probability. These are held-out test results, not training results. Differences show remaining calibration error.

Which inputs does the model rely on?

Increase in probability error when each input is shuffled in 2024 calibration data. Larger values mean the fitted model relies more on that input.

Averaged over five shuffles. Correlated inputs can share predictive information. This is global model dependence, not causation or an explanation of an individual result.

A defined cohort, not every rider

Eligible police forces had at least 95% injury-based reporting and at least 20 motorcycle casualties in each training year (2021–2023). Only injury-based records from those forces enter training, calibration and testing.

This reduces one source of recording inconsistency, but limits generalisation. The target is recorded KSI within that cohort, not the adjusted KSI estimate used elsewhere on the site.

Included police force areas

How the model was built

Logistic regression provides the simpler benchmark. The AI model contains 120 shallow boosted decision trees. Both use the same ten categorical inputs and receive probability calibration using 2024 only. Settings were fixed before the 2025 test. Records from a collision cannot cross the year-based splits.

No injury outcome, collision-severity field, severity-adjustment weight, casualty count, skid or impact information is supplied as a predictor. Training support and feature-importance checks do not use 2025 outcomes. A single later-year test does not establish future reliability.

The button evaluates the frozen fitted model locally. There is no chatbot, generated narrative or live retraining, and scenario selections are not sent to an AI service.

04 / TRANSPARENT METHODS

What is counted. What is known.

Download annual summary ↓

Source & scope

Department for Transport, STATS19 road safety open data: complete final annual collision, vehicle and casualty files for 2021–2025. Historical counts and national mileage rates (1979–2025) come from official table RAS0102. The data covers police-reported personal injury collisions on public roads in Great Britain. It is not a census of every collision or of Northern Ireland.

Official DfT data and release notes ↗

Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0. Source files retrieved 14 October 2026; this is a fixed snapshot, not a live feed.

Official historical and mileage tables ↗

Download source URLs and file hashes

Counting and joining

A collision is an event; a vehicle record is one involvement; a casualty is one injured or killed person. The main explorer counts motorcycle casualties, including passengers unless filtered.

Motorcycle casualties are selected by casualty type. Their own vehicle is joined using the text collision identifier and vehicle reference. Collision context is then joined once per collision. This avoids multiplying casualties by every vehicle in the same event.

Recent motorcycle codes: 2, 3, 4, 5, 23 and 97. E-scooters and pedal cycles are excluded. Five 2024 records disagree between casualty type (motorcycle) and vehicle type (other vehicle). We retain those casualties and their linked context, using casualty type for the explorer category. Collision-involvement figures use vehicle type.

Severity and denominators

Fatal casualties use the recorded fatal classification. Recorded KSI is fatal plus recorded serious casualties. Adjusted KSI is fatal plus the sum of the supplied serious-injury adjustment weights for nonfatal casualties. It is an estimate, so values can be fractional before rounding.

Category shares include unknown values. Percentage changes are changes in counts, not changes in collision risk. No mileage, licence-holder or fleet denominator is available in these three record-level files. National mileage rates are provided separately in Historical context from DfT RAS0102; they cannot be applied to filtered subgroups.

Filters describe casualty age and motorcycle category. They do not identify novice riders, CBT status, A1 licence holders or training participation.

Recording changes and uncertainty

Junction context uses valid historic codes where available, otherwise the current field. Bend status uses historic manoeuvre codes 16 and 17. A known different historic manoeuvre is distinct from missing bend information.

The headline year-on-year fatality comparison includes an approximate 95% Poisson count-ratio interval. It assumes independent counts and does not cover reporting bias, changing exposure or confounding. The separate AI research tab evaluates a predictive model in a restricted cohort. Neither section establishes causation.

Exploratory subgroup comparisons can be unstable and are not adjusted for multiple testing. Small counts are flagged for interpretation.

Data validation

Validation applies to the detailed motorcycle subset (2021–2025). Historical totals come from official table RAS0102. Recent casualty, fatal, serious and adjusted KSI totals reconcile to that table. These checks verify the processing, not the accuracy of every police record.
